data: firm rule sets; published cohort pass rate 0.168 (as cited in the abstract)
method: stage-by-stage incentive model, simulation
finding: Passing is a poor standalone signal of skill: position sizing alone gives a zero-skill pass probability near 0.40 against a measured cohort rate of 0.168, and a real edge and aggressive sizing move the pass probability by nearly the same amount.
relation: Closest prior work: same headline claim and zero-skill control; the paper must go beyond it (likelihood ratio, base rates, optimal-test benchmark).

method: chain of first-passage problems with six contract parameters; checked against simulation
finding: Success probability is derived in closed form (error below 1% against simulation); across 13 products with the same advertised target and buffer it varies by 62%, entirely from parameters published but not shown beside the price.
relation: Overlaps the mathematics of the trailing barrier; read in full before claiming any closed form.

method: arithmetic Brownian motion, Monte Carlo first-passage pricing with profit sweeps and fee refund
finding: A zero-edge trader passes the frictionless benchmark with probability 0.50 but the baseline contract with probability 0.30; contract value concentrates on a narrow risk-sizing ridge near 2 per cent daily volatility; model-implied average value of a USD 500 challenge is USD 221.
relation: Time limit as the main zero-edge penalty; two-step CFD contract. Check against firms with no time limit.

study_type: working paper (SSRN), hand-collected rule dataset + valuation
data: rule sets and fees displayed 25-26 July 2026 with dated screenshots
method: common benchmark population of skill and volatility, 300-day evaluation cap, one-year funded horizon
finding: At displayed list prices 29 of 31 contracts have negative benchmark expected value (before several restrictive terms are included, so estimates are upper bounds).
relation: Cross-firm rule table and expected value; benchmark for Sean's ten rule sets.

data: public rule pages observed 5 May 2026, eleven dimensions
method: systematic coding of rules
finding: A 5% daily and 10% maximum loss limit, an 80% base profit split, no time limit and MetaTrader connectivity each appear at a majority of firms; automated strategies are permitted in some form at 39 firms.
relation: Supports 'time limits are gone' and the rule-table inputs; no probability modelling.

method: mechanism design under asymmetric information; simple firm-profit-per-participant model
finding: Separates trading-funded from fee-funded revenue models and argues the dominant contemporary form is fee-funded, with consequences for the alignment of firm and participant incentives.
relation: Framing for why firms tolerate low pass rates; no simulation.

method: 10,000 randomised long/short paths; fixed-size strategy with symmetric 100-tick barriers
finding: Gross performance is about break-even (49.98% win rate), yet mean payouts of $9,368.50 exceed mean account costs of $7,878.30 (net $1,490.19 per account); 39.70% of full-sample simulations lose money.
relation: Zero edge can have positive expected value under the contract: the converse of the 'passers are skilled' reading.

method: closed-form analysis (from the title)
finding: No abstract in OpenAlex, Crossref or Semantic Scholar; not summarised.
relation: Hedged evaluation accounts with a static drawdown (title); read before citing.

data: 24-month exclusive observation, 490 manual and 510 AI-assisted traders
method: observational comparison, non-randomised
finding: AI-assisted traders show lower drawdowns (4.3% vs 7.8%), fewer emotionally driven exits (37.2% vs 61.7%) and a lower rule-breach rate (12.2% vs 18.4%); the author proposes a proprietary bias index.
relation: Low weight: vendor-linked, non-randomised; shows what behavioural data a firm holds.

data: retail traders on forex prop-firm platforms
method: sociology of finance (interpretive)
finding: Retail traders aim to become professional by passing the evaluation, but only a few succeed; the firms' main income is evaluation fees from the many who fail, secondary income is trading data from the few who succeed.
relation: Only peer-reviewed item on prop-firm challenges found; no model.

data: internal enrolment and performance records, sentiment analysis
method: benchmark comparison
finding: A 20% discount coupon is associated with higher enrolment and completion rates, modestly higher early-stage risk exposure and better medium-term retention.
relation: Price sensitivity of challenge buyers; single firm.

data: NASDAQ-100/SPY daily, Russell 3000 (as described in the note)
method: three predeclared gates, stationary bootstrap, Benjamini-Yekutieli, equivalence tests
finding: Four of six candidate retail signal families (oscillator, volume, calendar, candlestick) are refuted on statistical and/or economic materiality, trend and a momentum benchmark are inconclusive, none is supported.
relation: Methodological model (three-way verdict); also the nearest relative for paper 02.

method: volatility change between mid-year winners and losers
finding: Mid-year losers raise fund volatility in the later part of the assessment year more than winners, and the effect strengthens as industry growth and investor awareness rise.
relation: Tournament risk-shifting: the incentive logic behind a pass/fail threshold.

method: dynamic investment problem of a manager paid with a call option
finding: Under the optimal policy the option ends deep in or deep out of the money, but option compensation does not strictly lead to greater risk seeking; more options can reduce volatility.
relation: Capped downside plus profit share is an option; challenge fees cap the trader's loss.

method: semiparametric flow-performance estimation
finding: The shape of the flow-performance relationship creates incentives for managers to raise or lower fund risk depending on year-to-date standing.
relation: Convex payoffs and risk-taking incentives.

method: daily versus monthly volatility estimates
finding: With daily returns the monthly-data pattern of year-to-date underperformers raising risk disappears, suggesting earlier results were an artefact of inefficient monthly volatility estimates.
relation: Caution on tournament results; data-frequency artefact.

method: valuation of performance fees with high-water marks; closed-form cost of the mark
finding: Hedge-fund performance fees are valuable to managers and a claim on a significant share of investor wealth; high-water marks limit their value; a closed-form cost is derived under certain conditions.
relation: High-water-mark path dependence resembles the trailing drawdown.

method: regression of risk shifting on contract terms
finding: Risk shifting after poor performance is weaker when pay is tied to the high-water mark, when liquidation risk is low and when the manager has a large personal stake.
relation: How contract terms change risk-taking.

method: analysis of gaming of performance measures
finding: If a principal judges an agent with a performance measure, the agent has an incentive to game it (abstract truncated in the record).
relation: A pass rate is a measure that can be gamed by reshaping the return distribution.

data: 66,465 households at a large discount broker, 1991-96
method: account-level returns by turnover
finding: Households that trade most earn 11.4% a year against 17.9% for the market; the average household earns 16.4% and turns over 75% of its portfolio; overconfidence can explain the heavy trading and poor performance.
relation: Base rate: active retail trading lowers wealth.

data: complete trading history of all investors
method: aggregate portfolio performance
finding: The aggregate portfolio of individual investors suffers an annual performance penalty of 3.8 percentage points (2.2% of GDP); virtually all losses come from aggressive orders; institutions gain 1.5 points.
relation: Base rate: retail traders lose in aggregate.

method: two profitability methodologies
finding: About twice as many day traders lose money as make money; roughly 20 percent are more than marginally profitable; profitability relates to Nasdaq Composite movements.
relation: Share of day traders with positive results.

method: natural experiment from a margin-reduction day-trading policy
finding: Day traders incur an average significant loss of NT$61,500 after transaction costs (NT$26,700 before costs) over the sample period.
relation: Day-trader losses with a clean identification of day traders.

method: not stated in the record
finding: No abstract in OpenAlex, Crossref or Semantic Scholar; not summarised.
relation: Source for the share of day traders with persistent skill; read before quoting.

method: not stated in the record
finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: Emotion and trading performance among day traders; read before citing.

finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: Learning from trading experience; read before citing.

data: trading records of UK individual investors, 2006-2009
method: account-level analysis of stop-loss use
finding: Stop losses used as part of investment decisions are an effective tool against the disposition effect; stop-loss users have less experience.
relation: Stop-losses and retail behaviour.

data: over three years of trading data on 7,200 investors
method: multivariable regression
finding: Frequent trading is positively associated with being male, younger, using stop losses and using multiple trading channels.
relation: Who overtrades.

method: event-style analysis around large jackpots
finding: When jackpots exceed NT$500 million, trading volume falls 5.2% to 9.1% in stocks preferred by individuals, consistent with trading as a substitute for gambling.
relation: Trading as gambling; relevant to challenge buyers.

method: weighted latent class analysis
finding: Three subgroups of retail investors are found, the largest being crypto-traders (52.4%); the paper compares involvement, impulsivity, cognitive biases and problem gambling across them.
relation: Gambling overlap in retail traders.

method: not stated
finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: Day traders compared with gamblers.

data: one proprietary day trader at Bursa Malaysia
method: single-case study
finding: Contrasting with the literature on failed traders who trade actively and speculatively, the successful proprietary trader studied is described as highly attentive (abstract truncated in the record).
relation: A single success case, not evidence on base rates.

data: trade-by-trade records of retail, foreign institutional and proprietary traders
method: new discipline measures, profitability regressions
finding: Constructs trade-level measures of trading discipline and examines whether more disciplined traders are more profitable (abstract truncated).
relation: Discipline and profit; includes proprietary traders.

method: comparison of leverage rules (Kelly, optimal fraction)
finding: Leverage can increase profit in a popular day-trading strategy; the article relates it to the Kelly criterion and the optimal fraction criterion.
relation: Sizing and leverage: the lever that drives pass probability.

method: out-of-sample test of take-profit and stop-loss exits
finding: Taking profit after three consecutive bullish (bearish) one-minute candlesticks yields a notable positive average profit per trade, robust out of sample in an upward trend.
relation: Take-profit/stop-loss exits in a retail setting; check for data-snooping.

data: four market and nine sector ETFs, 2001-2021
method: trailing stop-loss rules with fixed and volatility-based thresholds
finding: Thresholds of 1.0 to 1.5 standard deviations give significantly higher excess returns; most trailing stop-loss strategies post positive excess returns after costs and risk.
relation: Trailing stops as a rule; Sean's trailing drawdown is the mirror image.

method: Laplace-transform solution of two-sided first passage for a Markov process
finding: Solves the first passage problem for a continuous Markov process leaving an interval; from the distribution of the exit time it deduces the distribution of the maximum and the range.
relation: Classical double-barrier exit law underlying the challenge pass/fail.

method: drawdowns and rallies of Brownian motion
finding: Determines the probability that a drawdown of a units precedes a rally of b units and applies it to stock-market crashes and rallies in the geometric Brownian motion model.
relation: Closest published statement of the trailing-drawdown challenge.

method: distribution of the maximum drawdown of Brownian motion with drift
finding: Gives an infinite-series representation of the distribution of the maximum drawdown and its expectation; the limiting behaviour is logarithmic (positive drift), square root (zero drift) or linear.
relation: Survival in the funded stage.

method: stopped diffusions with drawdown/drawup stopping times
finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: General-diffusion version of drawdown stopping results.

method: drawdowns and rallies with a finite horizon
finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: Same question as Hadjiliadis-Vecer with a deadline.

method: optimal investment under a drawdown constraint
finding: For constant relative risk aversion, the optimal policy invests in risky assets in proportion to the surplus between wealth and a fraction alpha of its running maximum.
relation: Investing under a drawdown constraint (the skilled trader's side).

method: growth-optimal portfolio under non-linear drawdown constraints (semimartingale model)
finding: Solves the long-term growth problem under a drawdown constraint by showing it equals an unconstrained problem with a modified utility.
relation: Extends Grossman-Zhou.

method: Conditional Drawdown risk measure
finding: Introduces conditional drawdown (CDD), the mean of the worst (1-alpha) drawdowns, with Maximal and Average Drawdown as limits and efficient optimisation techniques.
relation: Drawdown as a risk measure.

method: sensitivities to running maximum and maximum drawdown
finding: Defines new Greeks for sensitivities to the running maximum and maximum drawdown, relevant to hedge-fund net asset value and performance fees.
relation: High-water-mark contracts as derivatives.

method: stop-outs under serial correlation
finding: On average the recovery from a maximum quantile loss spans three times the period of accumulating it (the triple penance rule); the framework is generalised to first-order autocorrelation.
relation: Stop-out thresholds for managers.

method: continuity correction for discrete barrier options
finding: Discrete barrier options can be priced with remarkable accuracy using continuous-barrier formulas after a simple shift of the barrier.
relation: Why end-of-day-only breach checks raise zero-edge pass rates.

method: maximise probability of reaching a wealth goal by a deadline
finding: Finds the policy that maximises the probability of reaching a given wealth level by a fixed terminal time with n risky assets and a riskless one (generalising Kulldorff and Heath).
relation: Bold play as the way to hit a profit target.

method: four stop-loss implementations with overnight gaps and flash-crash drops
finding: Analyses the performance of four popular stop-loss implementations for asset prices modelled with overnight gaps and momentary price drops (abstract truncated).
relation: Stop-loss efficacy under gaps; relevant to breach at the stop.

method: minimising the probability of ruin for a firm with random risk process
finding: Solves for investment strategies that minimise the risk of ruin when bankruptcy risk cannot be eliminated.
relation: Ruin-minimising investment.

method: Bayesian Kelly strategy
finding: For log utility with an unobserved drift, the optimal bet is a fraction of wealth linear in the posterior mean increment (a generalised Kelly strategy).
relation: Sizing under uncertainty about edge.

method: double barrier options by path counting
finding: Gives analytic valuation formulas for options with two barriers (including rebates) using only defining properties of Brownian paths.
relation: Double-barrier exit mathematics in the option-pricing literature.

method: double barrier options via Laplace transforms
finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
relation: Double-barrier option pricing.

finding: No abstract available; not summarised.
